description_full: Northpointe Bancshares, Inc. operates as the bank holding company for Northpointe Bank provides various banking products and services in the United States. It operates through two segments: Mortgage Purchase Program and Retail Banking. The company offers digital deposit banking, such as noninterest-bearing accounts, savings, money-market demand accounts, and certificates of deposits; personal and business banking; and health saving accounts; home loans; mortgage purchase program; residential mortgage lending; and custodial deposit services. Northpointe Bancshares, Inc. was incorporated in 1998 and is headquartered in Grand Rapids, Michigan.

financial_summary: Northpointe Bancshares, Inc. is a small-cap financial services business with a $534M market cap on $242M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +29% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +6.7pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 85% against a 9% cost of capital — a 75-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $42M in free cash flow — roughly 17 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.53×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 0.5× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 20.8% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 33% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
